stories.headline: Russian strike on Kyiv arms depot kills dozens and sparks wide evacuations
stories.body:
Russian drones struck a Ukrainian military ammunition depot near Kyiv on Friday night [c1, c2]. The BBC reported that 37 people died [c1], while Al Jazeera reported 38 people died [c10]. The BBC said that 42 people were injured, including four children [c3]. Al Jazeera said that dozens of people were wounded [c10]. The explosion happened in the Bucha district on the outskirts of Kyiv [c1, c3]. The warehouse was in Myla and belonged to the Ukrainian military [c5, c22]. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed that the depot stored shells, drones, and other munitions [c22]. The strike caused stored shells, mines, and drones to explode late on Friday [c2]. More than 370 people were evacuated from the surrounding area [c20]. The BBC said almost 400 people were evacuated [c1].

The explosions damaged a care home for elderly and disabled people [c2]. Tymur Tkachenko, head of the local regional military administration, said the strike started a fire that damaged at least 50 residential buildings [c12]. Ukrainian media cited Tkachenko as saying 34 of the victims were residents at the care facility [c13]. Taras Didych, head of the Dmytrivka community, died while trying to rescue others during the explosion [c19]. Russia's Ministry of Defence said its forces targeted an ammunition depot containing launch boosters and drone parts [c5].

Ukrainian leaders criticized the decision to store weapons near homes [c4, c7]. President Zelensky said storing explosives next to residential areas was terrible negligence [c4]. He said criminal proceedings had been opened [c4]. Ukrainian Prime Minister Sergiy Koretsky said repeating storage mistakes in the fifth year of the full-scale invasion is criminal negligence [c7]. This was the second strike on a Kyiv munitions depot in less than two months [c11]. An earlier strike hit an ammunition warehouse in Vyshneve in July [c6]. The BBC said that July explosion killed nine people, injured dozens, and damaged over 280 homes [c6]. Prime Minister Koretsky said 22 people died in that July attack [c14]. An investigation showed a state-owned company broke rules about storing explosives near homes [c21]. President Zelensky said two officials from state-owned companies, including arms maker Ukroboronprom, would be held accountable for illegal storage [c15].

Attacks hit other regions as well [c9, c16]. Kyiv Mayor Vitaliy Klitschko said a two-year-old child died after a Russian drone crashed in Obolonskyi [c8]. Regional administration head Oleksandr Prokudin said Russian strikes on Kherson on Saturday killed two people and wounded 27 others [c16]. The Ukrainian army said it shot down 233 Russian drones overnight [c9]. Pavlo Palisa, deputy head of Ukraine's presidential office, said Ukrainian interceptor drones are not yet effective enough against jet-powered Russian drones [c17]. President Zelensky said Ukraine aims to launch 1,000 long-range drone strikes on Russia every day [c18].

vocab.meaning: failure to take proper care in doing something
an aircraft or drone designed to catch and destroy enemy targets

stories.headline: Niger military moves to stop army mutiny in capital city Niamey
stories.body:
Niger's military moved to stop a mutiny by rebel soldiers in the capital city of Niamey [c23, c26]. Rebellious troops attacked military officers, held soldiers hostage at a barracks, and fired at key sites [c26, c33]. Witnesses reported heavy gunfire and explosions at Base 101 shortly after midnight on Saturday [c34]. Rebel soldiers tried to enter the presidential palace and blocked the national television broadcaster Tele Sahel [c29, c32]. The channel went off the air for just over an hour before resuming broadcasts around 10:00 a.m. local time [c28, c32].

Niger's defence ministry said armed forces were retaking control of targeted sites [c27]. Diplomatic and security sources said the presidential guard, aided by Russian forces, recaptured an air base and killed several mutineers by Saturday evening [c30]. But regional sources said rebelling troops still held two barracks around Niamey on Saturday [c31].

This mutiny was the third major incident at the capital's airport complex in 2026 [c24]. Jihadists had previously attacked the airport twice earlier in the year [c36]. General Abdourahamane Tiani seized power in Niger in 2023, cutting ties with Western partners and aligning with Russia [c25]. Neighbouring Algeria condemned the mutiny and offered support to Niger's government [c35].

vocab.meaning: an open rebellion against authority by military forces
soldiers or sailors who take part in a rebellion

stories.headline: Rescuers search for thousands after Himalayan flood disaster kills hundreds
stories.body:
Rescuers searched for thousands of missing people across Nepal, India, and China after massive flash floods [c39, c41, c46]. The US Geological Survey said a massive glacial collapse caused the high-altitude disaster, sending debris torrents downstream [c46]. The confirmed death toll reached 682 people, including 675 in Nepal and seven in Tibet [c41]. Disaster agencies said nearly 3,000 people are missing [c39]. This includes 2,426 missing people in Nepal and 554 in Tibet [c39]. The missing list includes at least 777 foreign nationals and 933 hydropower project workers [c40]. The Red Cross estimated that the disaster affected at least 93,000 people, while over 3,700 people were rescued in Nepal [c42].

Rescue operations focused heavily on trapped workers [c43, c44]. The Nepali army pumped air through pipes into tunnels at the Trishuli 3A and 3B hydropower sites [c43]. Nepalese Energy Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha said workers drilled a hole into a cable tunnel, but could not reach trapped staff [c44]. Nepal asked for specialized foreign help, including tunnel rescue teams, tracking tech, DNA analysis tools, and mortuary facilities [c37]. India sent an 11-member technical team for tunnel rescue, and a Chinese team was expected soon [c38].

Several countries took action to aid victims and locate citizens [c45, c53, c55]. Indian authorities said they rescued 88 Indian nationals in Nepal, including four hydropower workers in Rasuwa [c53]. India's Ministry of External Affairs reduced its figure of missing Indian citizens in Nepal to 287 on Saturday [c51]. The ministry said another 128 uncontactable people in Nepal were of Indian origin with other nationalities [c52]. On Saturday, 120 Indian nationals crossed from Tibet into Nepal [c54]. In Tibet, Chinese authorities at Gyirong port evacuated 555 tourists and moved 499 local residents and workers to safety [c55]. Chinese monitors confirmed that a dammed debris lake started draining naturally, reducing immediate flood risks [c56].

The international response and climate concerns drew attention [c45, c48, c49]. The US State Department promised $500,000 in initial emergency aid for Nepal [c45]. Nepalese Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi agreed to share satellite and water data in real time [c47]. Khanal noted that Nepal produces only about 0.01 percent of global greenhouse gas emissions despite facing severe impacts [c48]. UN climate chief Simon Stiell said burning fossil fuels warms the climate and makes mountain disasters more frequent and severe [c49]. Meanwhile, flood survivors in Nuwakot district publicly criticized the Nepalese government for slow relief delivery and search efforts [c50].

vocab.meaning: relating to or caused by large masses of ice
relating to the movement and distribution of water
relating to scientific tests used to solve crimes or identify remains

stories.headline: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat speaks at New York event amid local protests
stories.body:
RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat spoke at a diaspora event at Madison Square Garden in New York [c57]. He delivered the keynote address at the Universal Oneness Celebration, supported by over 200 Hindu American groups [c57, c63]. Bhagwat said that if any Hindu believes Muslims should not live in India, that person is no longer a Hindu [c58]. He said RSS volunteers run about 130,000 service projects and increased dialogue with Muslim and Christian communities starting in 2018 [c61, c62]. To highlight equal service, he cited volunteer work after the 1996 Charkhi Dadri plane crash in Haryana [c59].

Bhagwat arrived in the United States on Tuesday for a centenary outreach tour across North America and the UK [c66]. He also spoke to leaders at the One World, One Humanity conference on August 29 [c60].

The visit drew strong pushback [c64, c65, c67]. Civil rights, interfaith, and caste groups protested outside Madison Square Garden [c67]. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani opposed the event, calling the group's ideology exclusionary [c64]. The US Commission on International Religious Freedom recommended revoking Bhagwat's visa and sanctioning RSS members [c65]. Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi previously spoke to 50,000 people at a 2019 event in Texas [c68].

vocab.meaning: a group of people living outside their ancestral homeland

stories.headline: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi arrives in Uzbekistan for regional summit tour
stories.body:
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi arrived in Uzbekistan on Saturday to start a two-nation Central Asian tour [c69]. Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev personally greeted Modi at Tashkent airport late at night [c73]. Modi's plane flew through Chinese airspace because Pakistan kept its airspace closed to Indian planes [c74]. This trip is Modi's fourth official visit to Uzbekistan, following visits in 2015, 2016, and 2022 [c78].

Modi said he plans to discuss trade, investment, defense, and energy with President Mirziyoyev [c70]. His schedule in Tashkent included visiting the Shastri Memorial, laying flowers at Yangi Uzbekistan Park, and visiting Tashkent State University [c71, c75]. Uzbekistan hosts over 18,000 Indian residents, including about 16,000 medical students [c76].

Modi will later attend the 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Bishkek and the World Nomad Games in Kyrgyzstan [c69, c77]. India's Ministry of External Affairs said Modi will meet Russian President Vladimir Putin during the summit [c72]. The ten-nation group covers 36 million square kilometers and over 3.4 billion people [c79]. The bloc represents about 25 percent of global economic output and over 15 percent of world trade [c80].

vocab.meaning: a planned route or list of activities for a trip
